text:
Bitcoin stabilized in the $60,700–$61,500 band on the morning of June 25, consolidating after a brief dip below $60,000 triggered $1 billion in long liquidations. Institutional sentiment remains fractured; while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs hemorrhaged a staggering $469 million, XRP spot ETFs contrarily captured $2.05 million in net inflows. This rotation occurs as the European regulatory landscape tightens, with only 210 of an estimated 3,000 firms securing EU MiCA authorization ahead of next week's July 1 deadline.

Broader macro conditions present a mixed backdrop for digital assets. Global equities rebounded overnight—led by Asian markets reacting to Micron Technology's blockbuster earnings—while the U.S.-Iran ceasefire accord drove crude oil prices lower. Consequently, sovereign bond yields flattened, with the 2-year Treasury steadying at 4.15% as global liquidity sidelines ahead of today's pivotal U.S. PCE inflation release.
